page: PDF p.19 (printed xv) and PDF p.54 (printed 30)
evidence: Preface, PDF p.19: "ANALYTICAL (Axis 3, measurement status) — arithmetic on stated inputs (roofline, KV-residency and capacity screens, the C/W per-host bound (C = per-host KV-slot capacity, W = mean KV-residency time) and the host counts derived from it)".  Ch. 2, PDF p.54: "The symbol is Mweights, not W: throughout the book W is reserved for mean time in system in Little's law, written Lexec = λWexec (Ch 4)."
issue: The symbol W is given two mutually exclusive definitions inside the same book, and the second one (Ch. 2) is the stronger, explicitly book-wide reservation. Ch. 2 asserts W is reserved for 'mean time in system' in Little's law; the Preface's evidence panel assigns W = 'mean KV-residency time' in the C/W per-host capacity bound. Because the C/W bound is the per-host capacity screen that produces every host count in Ch. 16–17, a reader following the Preface would compute with a different W than Ch. 2 sanctions, and cannot tell whether 'KV-residency time' and 'time in system' are meant to be the same quantity (the book elsewhere treats Wexec = 8.58 s as excluding the ~120 ms retrieval term).
fix_instruction: Choose one definition of W and apply it book-wide. Recommended: keep W = mean time in system (Little's law) as Ch. 2 states, and edit the Preface panel to read 'W = mean time in system (Wexec in the canonical scenario)'. If 'mean KV-residency time' is genuinely a distinct quantity, give it its own symbol (e.g. W_res) and state in Ch. 17 how it relates to Wexec. Add one sentence to Ch. 2 §2.3 or Ch. 17 Table 17-1 pinning the identity so the two chapters cannot drift.

evidence: Fig. 6.1 caption, PDF p.146: "Figure-art note: the third printed entry in the workload box (concurrency) is an erratum in the figure art for the offered request rate λ; it is not a workload metric. Concurrency proper is derived on the serving side (in-flight = λ × W, Little's law), the same classification this figure gives queue depth; see §6.1.1."  And §6.1.1, PDF p.144: "Concurrency is not a workload input: it is a serving-side quantity derived from the arrival rate and the time in system (Little's law), so it belongs with queue depth on the scheduler side, not in this layer."
issue: The rendered Fig. 6.1 artwork still prints 'concurrency' inside the 'Workload metrics' box, directly contradicting §6.1.1's classification and the figure's own causal chain (workload → resource → serving). The defect is patched only in the caption prose, so the figure itself — the artifact most readers will extract, redraw, or cite — carries the wrong taxonomy entry. The book treats this figure as the spine of its diagnostic method (Ch. 6 is the metrics chapter; Fig. 6.1 is referenced from Ch. 12's optimization map and the pattern library), so an unfixed artwork error propagates.
fix_instruction: Regenerate Fig. 6.1 so the workload box lists the offered quantities only (rps / request rate λ, token profile), and either move 'in-flight requests (λ·W)' into the serving box next to queue depth or drop it. Then delete the 'Figure-art note' erratum sentence from the caption, so the figure and its legend no longer disagree. If the artwork cannot be regenerated for this edition, restate the erratum as a visible on-figure footnote rather than caption text only.

page: PDF p.21 (printed xvii), PDF p.27 (printed 3), PDF p.79 (printed 55)
chapter: Preface (Reading conventions) / Ch. 1 (§1.1.2) / Ch. 4 (§4.3 canonical box) — targets in Appendix A
evidence: Preface, PDF p.21: "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N."  Ch. 1, PDF p.27: "all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10)".  Ch. 4, PDF p.79: "Appendix A's §A.7 (Fig A.2, vendor-relative KV/compute ratios) is its deliberate relaxation, not a correction."  Preface, PDF p.21 again: "a superseding re-verification of the DeepSeek model-service status (Appendix A, A.3) is carried under v20260913+addendum-20261101" and "Appendix A, A.6 carries a boxed 2026-09-27 capability probe".
issue: Appendix A sections are referenced in four mutually incompatible forms: '§9A' (letter suffix on a bare number, the form the Preface defines), '§10' (bare number, no letter suffix — violates the stated convention), '§A.7' (figure-style 'A.N' label applied to a section), and 'A.3' / 'A.6' (figure-style labels used for sections with no § marker at all). The Preface explicitly fixes one convention and the body then departs from it three different ways. A reader following 'Appendix A §10' or 'Appendix A's §A.7' cannot tell whether these denote the section labelled 9A-style, a numbered section, or a figure, and 'Fig A.2' sits next to '§A.7' inside the same phrase, compounding the ambiguity.
fix_instruction: Pick one Appendix A labelling scheme and apply it to the appendix itself and to every reference. Either (a) label appendix sections 1, 2, 3 … and reference them as 'Appendix A §3', 'Appendix A §7', 'Appendix A §10' while figures keep 'Fig A.N'; or (b) keep letter-suffixed sections ('9A') and reference them as 'Appendix A §9A' only. Remove the '§' from the two bare-figure-style references ('Appendix A, A.3' → 'Appendix A §3' or the correct section label; 'Appendix A, A.6' likewise) and fix the Preface sentence to state the single rule, including whether 'A.N' is figures-only.

page: PDF p.20 (printed xvi), PDF p.100 (printed 76), PDF p.104 (printed 80)
chapter: Preface (Evidence boundary) / Ch. 4 (Table 4-2 and its Note 1)
evidence: Preface, PDF p.20: "Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair (e.g. [1P][DERIVED]); Axis 3, measurement status, rides along where a claim's status is known."  Ch. 4 Note 1, PDF p.104: "Axis 3 measurement status — how far it has climbed the measurement hierarchy: ANALYTICAL / SCENARIO-DERIVED / MODELED / MEASURED, or UNMEASURED." and "SCENARIO-DERIVED is the Axis-3 stage a canonical-scenario value normally reports."  Table 4-2 row, PDF p.100: "Execution occupancy | ~86 / ~344 requests (at Wexec ≈ 8.6 s ...) | [canonical scenario][DERIVED] Little's Law L = λ × Wexec" — two tags only, no Axis-3 tag.
issue: The book declares its own Axis-3 rule twice — the Preface requires Axis 3 to ride along with the label pair, and Ch. 4's Note 1 states that SCENARIO-DERIVED is the Axis-3 status a canonical-scenario value 'normally reports' — but canonical-scenario values are then labelled with two tags only. Every row of the canonical-scenario provenance ledger (Table 4-2) and the derived canonical values carried through Ch. 1, Ch. 4, Ch. 6, Ch. 7 and Ch. 17 omit Axis 3, even though the book elsewhere uses standalone Axis-3 tags in prose ('That figure is an ANALYTICAL floor screen, not a measurement', PDF p.158; 'SCENARIO-DERIVED is the Axis-3 stage a canonical-scenario value normally reports'). As written, a canonical-scenario value is formally unlabelled on Axis 3, so a reader cannot distinguish a canonical-scenario-derived figure from an ANALYTICAL bound from the label pair alone.
fix_instruction: Either apply the declared rule — add the third tag to canonical-scenario rows and derived values (e.g. '[canonical scenario][DERIVED][SCENARIO-DERIVED]' in Table 4-2 and the values derived from it) — or, if Axis 3 is deliberately optional for canonical-scenario values, amend the Preface and Note 1 to say so explicitly (e.g. 'Axis 3 is implied by the provenance tag for [canonical scenario] values and stated explicitly only for ANALYTICAL/MEASURED claims'). Whichever way, make the two statements consistent so a reader can apply one rule.

page: PDF p.98 (printed 74), PDF p.112 (printed 88), PDF p.115 (printed 91)
chapter: Ch. 4 (§4.3 economic sidebar and Economic Constraints)
evidence: Sidebar cell, PDF p.98: "capex amortized: 21 × ($350K capex ÷ 60 mo = $5,833.3333 + $1,110.33 energy) = $145,816.93, + $10,000 fixed staff (Ch 16) — owned, not rented, so ~half the cloud 21-host line."  §4.3, PDF p.112: "So the owned per-request cost is computed whole-fleet as (N_hosts × $20/hr) ÷ (rps × 3600) ≈ (6 × $20) ÷ (10 × 3600) ≈ ~$0.0033 per request at average" — where $20/hr is the cloud on-demand rental price.  Reconciliation note, PDF p.115: "the self-host 21-host line is a separate $155,816.93/month and is a distinct owned capex+energy cost basis, not a point in this cloud-rental series".
issue: The word 'owned' carries two different meanings inside Ch. 4. In the $0.0033/$0.0140/$0.0029/$0.0056 per-request figures, 'owned fleet' means the fleet you operate yourself — and is explicitly computed from the cloud on-demand rental price of ~$20/hr, i.e. a rented fleet. In the sidebar and reconciliation note, 'owned' is used for the self-hosted capex+energy+staff total, and is contrasted with the cloud line as 'owned, not rented'. The same adjective therefore marks both the cloud-rental basis and its opposite within one chapter, while the chapter repeatedly warns that these figures are 'never cross-compared'. A reader quoting 'owned-fleet basis' cannot tell which of the two cost lines is meant.
fix_instruction: Reserve 'owned' for the self-hosted capex+energy+staff line and rename the other basis consistently — e.g. 'self-operated fleet basis (rented GPU instances)' for the $0.0033/$0.0140/$0.0029/$0.0056 family, and 'self-host basis' for the $155,816.93 line. Update the six-figure reconciliation table's Basis column labels and the sidebar's 'owned, not rented' wording so the two terms cannot be read as the same thing.
